title: MoltbookResponseIntakeRecord
description: One record per response received to the Moltbook first-contact post (see MOLTBOOK_FIRST_CONTACT/POST.md and FOLLOWUP_PROTOCOL.md). Every response is logged as one of these, honestly, including noise and hostile responses -- classification is not a filter for what gets kept, only for how it's read. NOTE ON ENFORCEMENT: JSON Schema validation alone cannot enforce the cross-field rule that attribution.may_attribute_publicly may only be true when consent.consent_given is 'explicit_yes' -- that rule is documented on both fields below, but whatever intake tooling writes these records is responsible for actually enforcing it before publication; schema validity does not by itself guarantee consent was respected.

response_id.description: Unique identifier for this intake record, independent of any platform-native id.

category.description: Primary classification. See FOLLOWUP_PROTOCOL.md section 1 for definitions. A response that could plausibly fit more than one category still gets exactly one primary category here; use secondary_category for the runner-up, not a forced merge.

secondary_category.description: Optional runner-up classification when a response genuinely straddles two categories.

classification_confidence.description: How confident the classifier (human or agent) is in `category`. Values below 0.6 should be treated as needing a second look before factoring into selection (FOLLOWUP_PROTOCOL.md section 2) -- this is uncertainty about OUR reading of the response, not about the response's own validity.

content_uncertainty.description: Uncertainty about the response's own content or provenance, kept separate from classification_confidence (which is about our interpretation, not the source).

provenance_confidence.description: Confidence that the provenance fields below (handle, platform, timestamp) are accurate -- e.g. lower if hand-transcribed from a screenshot than if pulled via API.

provenance.description: Where this response came from, preserved even if the response is later anonymized for publication -- anonymization affects what's SHOWN, never what's RECORDED internally.

venue.description: e.g. 'm/agents'. Should always be m/agents for responses to the initial post per the no-cross-posting boundary.

responder_handle.description: Public handle/display name as it appeared on the platform, verbatim.

responder_platform_id.description: Platform-internal stable id, if available, distinct from the (changeable) display handle.

capture_method.description: How this record was captured. Affects content_uncertainty.provenance_confidence.

in_reply_to.description: response_id or platform id of the record this is a reply to, if this is part of a thread rather than a top-level response.

raw_text.description: Verbatim text of the response as posted. Never paraphrased at capture time -- paraphrasing, if any, happens only downstream in a follow-up report and is a separate field there.

media_refs.description: References/links to any non-text media attached to the response (images, code, video). Not fetched or embedded here -- referenced only.

attribution.description: Whether and how this responder may be credited if their response is used in a follow-up report (FOLLOWUP_PROTOCOL.md section 4). Governed entirely by `consent` below -- this object records the RESULT of applying the consent rule, not an independent judgment call.

may_attribute_publicly.description: True only if consent.consent_given is 'explicit_yes'. Defaults to false otherwise -- silence, ambiguity, or absence of a response to a consent ask is never treated as yes.

display_name_if_attributed.description: Exact form of attribution to use, if may_attribute_publicly is true (may differ from responder_handle, e.g. a preferred name given explicitly).

anonymized_label.description: Non-identifying label to use instead, when may_attribute_publicly is false but the response is still referenced (e.g. 'a Moltbook responder').

consent.description: The actual consent state this record was given, as the source of truth for `attribution` above.

consent_given.description: 'unclear' and 'not_asked' MUST both resolve to attribution.may_attribute_publicly = false. Only 'explicit_yes' may resolve to true.

consent_scope.description: What the responder agreed to, if anything. 'internal_use_only' means the response may inform ForgeWorld's thinking but must never appear, even anonymized, in a public follow-up.

selection.description: Tracks this response's status against FOLLOWUP_PROTOCOL.md section 2's selection process. Proposing eligibility/selection is something an agent may do; setting selected=true as final requires James's confirmation per FOLLOWUP_PROTOCOL.md section 5, recorded in selection_notes.

eligible_for_selection.description: Whether this response is specific and falsifiable enough to be a candidate for the one selected challenge (categories counterexample, adversarial_test, and specific governance_concern responses are the usual candidates).

selected.description: True only after James has confirmed this as the one challenge acted on for this encounter.
